officialTitle: Efficacy of Selpercatinib in RET Fusion-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
setting: Advanced, previously platinum-treated and treatment-naive cohorts

design.blinding: Open-label; response by independent review committee

clinicalQuestion: What is the activity of the selective RET inhibitor selpercatinib in advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC, both after platinum chemotherapy and in untreated patients?

pico.population: Advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC, previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy or previously untreated
pico.outcomes: Primary: IRC-assessed ORR. Secondary: DoR, PFS, safety

publications.title: Efficacy of Selpercatinib inFusion-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary NSCLC analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: In the first 105 consecutively enrolled patients withfusion-positive NSCLC who had previously received at least platinum-based chemotherapy, the percentage with an objective response was 64% (95% confidence interval [CI], 54 to 73).
The median duration of response was 17.5 months (95% CI, 12.0 to could not be evaluated), and 63% of the responses were ongoing at a median follow-up of 12.1 months.
Among 39 previously untreated patients, the percentage with an objective response was 85% (95% CI, 70 to 94), and 90% of the responses were ongoing at 6 months.
Among 11 patients with measurable central nervous system metastasis at enrollment, the percentage with an objective intracranial response was 91% (95% CI, 59 to 100).

safety.experimentalValue: Hypertension 14%; ALT increase 12%; AST increase 10%; hyponatraemia 6%; lymphopenia 6%
safety.sourceQuote: The most common adverse events of grade 3 or higher were hypertension (in 14% of the patients), an increased alanine aminotransferase level (in 12%), an increased aspartate aminotransferase level (in 10%), hyponatremia (in 6%), and lymphopenia (in 6%).

safety.description: Discontinuation due to drug-related adverse event
safety.sourceQuote: A total of 12 of 531 patients (2%) discontinued selpercatinib because of a drug-related adverse event.

strengths: Both pretreated and treatment-naive cohorts with intracranial assessment

clinicalImplications.text: Established selective RET inhibition with selpercatinib as highly active in RET fusion-positive NSCLC, including intracranial disease.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Monitor blood pressure and liver enzymes on selpercatinib.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 32846060. Doses not printed in abstract.
